$description: ARIEL-only extension tokens: relevance-score badge colors (ariel-score-*). Source: ariel/static/css/variables.css lines 56-61 (dark) and 184-189 (light). ARIEL's own --color-amber/--font-sans etc. are NOT reproduced here — those are retired in Task 3.5 in favor of the canonical accent-secondary.*/font.display tokens; only the score-badge triplet is a genuine ARIEL-specific extension. Every score.* value here already coincides exactly with an existing ramp step used elsewhere (no new primitives needed). The high-contrast-dark/high-contrast-light groups are AUTHORED explicitly (not opted out) for two reasons: these badge foregrounds are genuine information-bearing text that must clear the family's AAA gates against its own more extreme bg.primary, and that family is fully monochrome — an inherited green/orange badge would be the one hue left on the page. The monochrome badges keep the score ladder as a lightness ladder (high = furthest from the canvas, low = closest), which is the same encoding the badge's own numeric label already carries.

low.$description: 7.37:1 vs high-contrast-dark's bg.primary — clears the AAA body-text floor even at the bottom of the ladder.

ariel-score.$description: AUTHORED rather than inherited, for the same reason the high-contrast groups are: the `desy` family is bound to the DESY Styleguide (06/24) palette and uses published hexes only, so an inherited generic green/amber badge would be the one off-brand hue on the page. The ladder keeps its green -> amber -> neutral semantics using DESY Green, DESY Yellow and the petrol neutral ramp.

medium.$description: DESY Yellow — 11.54:1; the styleguide's amber analogue, and the same hex this family uses for status.warning.

low.$description: Petrol neutral — 5.01:1; the canvas ramp's muted step, matching the neutral role slate.650 plays in the main family.

ariel-score.$description: AUTHORED rather than inherited — see the desy-dark group. DESY's palette has no dark green, so the `high` badge sits at the non-text tier (3.03:1); it is a short badge label over its own tint rather than body copy, and the numeric score it accompanies carries the same information independently.

high.$description: DESY Green — 3.03:1 vs desy-light's bg.primary; the palette's only green.

medium.$description: DESY accessibility orange — 2.90:1; DESY Yellow (1.47:1) and Olive (1.91:1) are far weaker on a near-white canvas, and Dark olive reads as green beside the `high` badge.
